newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open flat to slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open flat to slightly lower.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open unchanged to slightly weaker Friday, based on market orders at 1018 EST, dealers said.
Friday morning, USDA released its January world supply/demand data for 1996/97. It pegged U.S. cotton ending stocks at 4.70 million 480-lb bales, up from 4.70 million bales in its December estimate.
World ending stocks were seen by USDA at 36.82 million bales in January, down slightly from 36.96 million bales last month.

U.S. exports for 1996/97 were forecast at 6.30 million bales compared with 6.20 million bales seen a month ago. World exports were revised up to 26.89 million bales in January versus 26.33 million bales in the USDA's December report.
Prudential Securities cotton specialist Ernest Simon said the USDA data should have little effect on the futures market.
"It is a pretty neutral report," Simon said. "I do not see anything unexpected or unusual."
New York cotton futures finished slightly lower Thursday after the USDA raised its U.S. cotton crop estimate. March cotton settled down 0.40 cent at 73.56 cents a lb, traded 73.95 to to 73.54 cents.
Volume reached an estimated at 8,500 lots compared to Wednesday's 9,187 lots.

Thursday, USDA estimated U.S. 1996/97 cotton production at 18.951 480-lb bales, up one percent over the 18.738 million bales estimated in December. This would be the second largest production on record.
